    12	### C4-H-01: separate signing cutoff and withdrawal readiness
    13	
    14	`BLSAggregator-4.14.0` retains the two-day public notice. For request time `t`:
    15	
    16	- `readyAt = t + 2 days`: signing stops, exactly as before.
    17	- `withdrawAt = readyAt + GUARDIAN_FRAUD_CHALLENGE = t + 3 days`.
    18	- `expiresAt = withdrawAt + GUARDIAN_EXIT_WINDOW = t + 4 days`.
    19	- Withdrawal is permitted at both endpoints `[withdrawAt, expiresAt]`, absent a
    20	  pending case. `GuardianExitNotReady` now reports `withdrawAt`.
    21	- `GUARDIAN_SLASH_CASE_WINDOW = 5 days > 2 + 1 + 1 days`.
    22	  `VERIFIER_ROTATION_DELAY` remains tied to that constant and becomes five days.
    23	
    24	Every other use of the notice fields was checked:
    25	
    26	- `_reconstructPkAgg` is unchanged: a nonzero notice excludes its key from
    27	  `readyAt`, including throughout the challenge period and after `expiresAt`.
    28	  Expiry never silently restores a potentially fraudulent signer.
    29	- `_requireCommitteeSurvivesExit` already excludes all other announced exits,
    30	  even before their cutoff. It conservatively checks the eventual signer set;
    31	  delaying withdrawal does not change the set or weaken the quorum floor.
    32	- Cancellation deletes the notice, restores signing eligibility, and starts the
    33	  existing one-day cooldown. Pending cases still prohibit cancellation and new
    34	  notices. A cancelled notice cannot be consumed; a fresh notice incurs the full
    35	  notice and challenge again. Expired notices still require cancellation and
    36	  cooldown before replacement.
    37	- `consumeGuardianExit` still checks pending cases before timing, so a case queued
    38	  during the challenge freezes the guardian even after withdrawal would mature.
    39	  Successful consumption deletes the notice atomically with Registry role exit.
    40	- Any notice already open when a case is queued expires before that case's
    41	  five-day deadline. New notices are forbidden during a pending case. The old
    42	  comment suggesting an accused guardian could open a notice after queueing was
    43	  corrected rather than retained.
    44	- Fraud-verifier rotation retains its full-case-window delay and verdict pinning.
    45	  Request structs, event fields and storage layout are unchanged; the public
    46	  `readyAt` event/getter field still means signing cutoff, not withdrawal time.

    63	deferred C4-L-01 to 5.5.1; DSR then ruled it into rc.8, together with the typed keys and
    64	MAX_VALIDATORS = 64 (commit "typed replay/commitment keys, anchored signer commitments, MAX_VALIDATORS 64").
    65	- The generic path keys replay protection and its commitment by
    66	  `uint256(keccak256(abi.encode(TAG_PROPOSAL, proposalId)))`. The `markProposalExecuted` callback to
    67	  DVTValidator is removed, so a generic id can no longer pre-consume a slash id that DVTValidator allocates
    68	  later.
    69	- Raw slash and reputation ids must be below 2^128 (`InvalidProposalId`), which separates them from the
    70	  keccak-derived generic and queue keys by 128 bits.
    71	- Each path stores its commitment under its own key, and the commitment also binds
    72	  `blockhash(block.number - 1)`. Every write emits `SignersCommitted(key, signerMask)`.
    73	- MAX_VALIDATORS is 64, and slot 65 reverts with `SlotOutOfRange`.
    74	
    75	Tests that run on Prague with genuine keys:
    76	- both paths keep both commitments: test_QueueSlashGeneric_OverlappingInputsKeepAllCommitments;
    77	- the crafted collision: test_SlashRawIdEqualToGenericKeyCannotOverwriteGenericCommitment;
    78	- slot 65: test_RegisterBLSPublicKey_SlotAboveMax_Reverts, test_Verify_RejectsBitsBeyondMaxValidators;
    79	- the typed key per path in the recompute: test_QueueSlashGeneric_OverlappingInputsKeepAllCommitments,
    80	  test_GenericCommitmentIsStoredBeforeTargetCall.
    81	
    82	Version: `BLSAggregator-4.14.0`. Main had already carried `4.13.0` for the build with C4-L-01 deferred.
    83	That build was never deployed, but two bytecodes must not share a version.
    84	
    85	### C2-01: invalidate stale standby roles
    86	
    87	`_setCurrentSP` clears a matching designated standby and emits `StandbyInvalidated`.
    88	It separately clears a matching pending standby **and ETA**, emitting
    89	`StandbyProposalCancelled`. No storage was added. Designation activation rechecks
    90	both current SP and emergency-revoked SP after the timelock and before designation.
    91	Tests cover normal promotion of a designated standby, simultaneous mature SP and
    92	standby proposals, cancellation events/ETA clearing, and both activation guards.
    93	The latter seed stale state explicitly, since normal promotion now clears it.
    94	
    95	### C1-L-01: report the applied slash penalty
    96	
    97	`_slash` returns its final capped/clamped penalty. `executeSlashWithBLS` emits that
    98	value in `SlashExecutedWithProof`. The regression deposits 1,000 aPNTs and checks
    99	that a MAJOR slash emits 300, leaves 700, credits 300 revenue and records 300 in
   100	history. SuperPaymaster core/Admin storage is untouched.
   101	
   102	### Registry ENDUSER membership cleanup
   103	
   104	`MySBT.deactivateAllMemberships` cannot attribute a membership to the role that
   105	created it: it iterates every membership stored for the user's SBT and deactivates
   106	every active entry. Therefore `Registry.exitRole(ROLE_ENDUSER)` calls it only when
   107	`userRoleCount[user] == 0` after role removal. If another role remains, all
   108	memberships remain intact. In particular, a per-community membership can outlive
   109	the ENDUSER role while another role is held. Integrators must not treat
   110	`MySBT.verifyCommunityMembership(user, community)` as sufficient authorization;
   111	they must also require `Registry.hasRole(ROLE_ENDUSER, user)`.
   112	
   113	A later final-role exit burns the SBT and deactivates its memberships through
   114	`MySBT.burnSBT`. If a final non-ENDUSER exit occurs while MySBT is paused, the burn
   115	fails non-fatally and sets `pendingSBTBurn`; after unpausing MySBT, anyone can call
   116	`reconcileSBTBurn(user)`. The permissionless
   117	`reconcileMembershipDeactivation` retry applies the same zero-role condition, so
   118	a stale pending flag cannot deactivate memberships while any role remains. If a
   119	third party adds COMMUNITY, ANODE, DVT, KMS, PAYMASTER_AOA, or PAYMASTER_SUPER
   120	(e.g. via a community's `safeMintForRole`) before that retry, recovery requires
   121	the holder to exit every remaining role. COMMUNITY has a zero default lock; the
   122	operator roles use `block.timestamp >= lockedAt + 30 days` (and DVT also requires
   123	its guardian-exit authorization). Exit and reconciliation are separate
   124	transactions, so a sponsor that keeps funding grants can re-grant a role after
   125	each exit and before the retry, delaying recovery indefinitely while it keeps
   126	paying; recovery is therefore not bounded against an actively funded sponsor.
   127	Precondition for any of this: a MySBT cleanup call must first have FAILED
   128	(e.g. MySBT paused or replaced by a reverting implementation). Once `userRoleCount == 0`, call
   129	`reconcileMembershipDeactivation(user)`; if the final burn also failed, unpause
   130	MySBT and call `reconcileSBTBurn(user)`. ENDUSER registration remains blocked until
   131	the membership-cleanup flag is cleared.
   132	
   133	This is the documented fallback because the targeted cleanup implementation did
   134	not fit EIP-170: the round-6 Registry measured 24,509 B, a behavior-preserving
   135	counter simplification reclaimed 29 B (24,480 B), and the minimal implementation
   136	then measured 25,002 B, 426 B over the 24,576 B limit. The attempted code and
   137	reclamation were reverted.
   138	
   139	REG-R5-02 does not require a migration: the Sepolia Registry has never emitted
   140	`SBTBurnFailed` (verified by the evidence script on `cc125/rc8-reg-evidence`), and
   141	the Optimism deployment is fresh.
   142	
   143	### PolicyRegistry velocity and spend reads
   144	
   145	PolicyRegistry 3.0.2 rejects `setTargetVelocity` and `tightenTargetVelocity` while
   146	the target velocity window is zero. Disabling a window invalidates all prior
   147	per-asset limits; re-enabling it remains fail-closed until each asset receives a
   148	fresh timelocked `setTargetVelocity`, which also starts a fresh target counter.
   149	`getTargetVelocity` reports stale/disabled entries as unconfigured, and no setter
   150	or tightening event is emitted for a rejected zero-window call.
   151	
   152	`getAssetSpend` now returns effective spend (zero once its configured window has
   153	expired). The new `getTargetSpend(sender, target, asset)` returns the same
   154	window-aware value for target velocity, including zero for disabled, stale, or
   155	expired entries.
   156	
   157	### I3 release requirement
   158	
   159	Any future validation-time consumer of `PolicyRegistry` must pass the ERC-7562
   160	tracer gate before release. This is a documented release requirement even when
   161	the consumer's direct unit and integration tests pass.
   162

   179	## BLS round 4
   180	
   181	### DVT proposal-id rotation
   182	
   183	`DVTValidator-0.8.0` takes `(registry, firstProposalId)`; there is no predecessor
   184	argument or state. `firstProposalId` is nonzero and below `2^128`. The retained
   185	BLSAggregator-4.14.0 owns a monotonic `proposalFloor`. Activation atomically
   186	captures the outgoing DVT's next allocation, including pending IDs, and validates
   187	the successor's aggregator and Registry pointers. Every allocation reads that
   188	floor once. Empty intermediates and A→B→A rollback cannot reuse allocated IDs.
   189	The ordinary setter fails closed if the outgoing counter cannot be read. The
   190	explicit-floor recovery operation requires governance to supply an audited upper
   191	bound on all allocated IDs; it must never lower the stored floor. This recovery
   192	is an immediate owner authority, not automatic discovery of missing history.
   193	
   194	Pending slash and aggregator-routed reputation proposals executed through the
   195	current DVT need fresh IDs and proofs after rotation, including after reactivation.
   196	The floor does not revoke owner-direct `verifyAndExecute` with caller-chosen IDs,
   197	generic proofs, authorized direct Registry reputation proofs or unused consensus
   198	queue pre-flags; see the disclosed M1 residuals below. Full-width hashed
   199	ReputationSystem IDs remain valid on the direct Registry route.
   200	
   201	### Validator-removal quorum floor
   202	
   203	The survival check protects each currently reachable configured threshold:
   204	`minThreshold`, `defaultThreshold`, and every severity threshold. With one
   205	eligible signer leaving, crossing a threshold is exactly equality with the
   206	pre-exit committee count. Higher unreachable thresholds do not hide lower working
   207	ones; caller-selected generic thresholds above `minThreshold` are not standing
   208	configured quorums. At an exactly reachable N-of-N quorum, seat a replacement or
   209	change policy before voluntary exit or DVT removal. Direct owner revocation and
   210	suspension are explicit emergency overrides.
   211	
   212	Suspension is authoritative on the retained aggregator and is checked both during
   213	registration and while reconstructing every aggregate key. It survives rotation
   214	and rollback and can be set even without local admission or an active key. Use
   215	owner `revokeAndSuspend` for atomic emergency eviction. Reinstatement requires
   216	explicit owner clearance on the aggregator; DVT admission alone cannot clear it.
   217	
   218	The DVT and aggregator owners must remain the same Safe-compatible M-of-N owner.
   219	Rotation delegates key-registration authority as well as proposal forwarding;
   220	it is therefore more than the owner's existing direct execution permission.
   221	Verifier rotation separately retains its contract-enforced five-day delay.
   222	
   223	### Reputation rule disablement
   224	
   225	`Reputation-0.6.0` records rule existence and active state separately. A configured
   226	zero-base rule contributes no score and does not receive the default. Only an
   227	unconfigured first rule receives the default. Re-enabling does not duplicate an
   228	active rule. The additional mappings belong to a directly deployed contract;
   229	there is no proxy migration or automatic backfill claim.
   230	
   231	### NFT boost semantics
   232	
   233	NFT boost eligibility means **registration age plus current ownership**. The
   234	seven-day timestamp is not proof of uninterrupted ownership: a third-party NFT
   235	can be transferred away and reacquired before a permissionless watcher calls
   236	`resetNFTHoldStart`. Strict continuity is impossible here without collection
   237	transfer hooks, checkpoints, escrow, or authenticated acquisition history.
   238	
   239	### Raw-id separation wording
   240	
   241	Raw proposal ids remain below `2^128`. Their separation from unrestricted
   242	Keccak-derived generic and queue keys is a 128-bit cryptographic guarantee, not
   243	an absolute structural impossibility.
   244

   468	## Daybreak re-review #3 — SP-551-07 through SP-551-11
   469	
   470	A slash now reverts with `SlashBlockedByInflight` while the operator has any counted reservation.
   471	Consequently every successful owner or BLS slash uses the liquid balance, which at that point equals
   472	total collateral. BLS MINOR and MAJOR derive their percentage from that same balance. The guardian
   473	can only queue a freeze; it cannot execute a separate penalty route.
   474	
   475	Validation does not inspect slash state: `_isSlashPending` depends on `block.timestamp`, which
   476	ERC-7562 OP-011 forbids in every validation entity. A reservation is live only in its originating
   477	`handleOps` transaction. After that transaction it is stale and `releaseStaleSponsorship(opHash)` is
   478	callable by any address immediately. The owner path exposes the atomic
   479	`slashOperatorAfterReleasing` variant: it releases supplied stale hashes, retains the same
   480	`SlashBlockedByInflight` check, and slashes in one transaction. Hashes are recoverable from public
   481	`handleOps` calldata; omitting a live or unknown stale record fails closed at the aggregate guard.
   482	
   483	`Inflight.counted` was appended after the original packed fields. Records created before 5.5.1 read
   484	`false`, so settling or releasing one cannot subtract from the new aggregate. New records set it to
   485	`true` and decrement exactly once. This changes an internal mapping-value layout only; top-level UUPS
   486	slots and the storage gap are unchanged. `totalSpent` retains its 5.5.0 meaning: validation adds the
   487	reserved `a0`, and settlement never adds it again.
   488	
   489	Superseded by "Amsterdam gas floors (SP-c)" below: `GP_CPOSTOP_MIN` is now 450,000 and the release
   490	tuple is `(500000,450000,5000,450000)`; 480,000 is rejected. The pre-SP-c text (cPostop floor 180,000,
   491	release tuple `(480000,450000,5000,450000)`) is kept only as history and must not be executed. `SuperPaymasterLens.version()` and the
   492	release pin now report `SuperPaymasterLens-1.2.1`.
   493	
   494	The OP-011-corrected remeasurement is lower but does not relax that conservative floor: validation uses
   495	272,723 of the 1,150,000 verification budget (877,277 headroom), and the measured worst postOp path
   496	uses 132,091 gas. Its 15% requirement is 151,905, so release `cPostop=450000` has 317,909 raw gas
   497	headroom (24,067 bps over the measured path). The maximum measured entry-guard bound is 462,035,
   498	leaving 17,965 under the then-proposed `minPostOpGas=480000` (superseded: release is 500,000).
   499	
   500	## Critical OP-011 correction — 2026-11-10
   501	
   502	The earlier SP L-01 claim is withdrawn. Validation no longer writes
   503	`userOpState[operator][sender].lastTimestamp`; doing so executed `TIMESTAMP`, which ERC-7562 OP-011
   504	forbids regardless of stake and caused real bundlers to reject every sponsored UserOp. `postOp`
   505	remains the sole timestamp writer. Validation computes `validAfter` from that stored value, matching
   506	the pre-rc.8 V3.6 behavior.
   507	
   508	The author formally approved this best-effort behavior as the 5.5.1 release scope on 2026-11-10.
   509	The reason is that strict validation-time timestamp accounting would execute `TIMESTAMP`, which
   510	ERC-7562 OP-011 forbids. The accepted residual is that a malicious bundler or a staked sender can
   511	admit two same-sender operations in one bundle before either `postOp` stores the timestamp; every
   512	admitted operation still reserves and pays independently. Honest bundlers include at most one
   513	operation per unstaked sender in a bundle. The regression demonstrates the residual through direct
   514	EntryPoint v0.7 `handleOps` and checks that both operations settle and are charged.
   515	
   516	An optional per-`(operator, sender)` `TSTORE` same-bundle marker is deferred to 5.5.x. It is gated on
   517	a real ERC-7562 bundler validation tracer accepting the complete `TLOAD`/`TSTORE` path; it must not be
   518	added based only on a local opcode hand trace.
   519	
   520	An opcode-level Foundry trace now covers `minTxInterval` zero/nonzero, queued-slash admission, and
   521	credit fallback through real EntryPoint v0.7. It scans the SP proxy validation frame and its complete
   522	call/delegatecall closure for OP-011 opcodes, and enforces OP-012 by allowing `GAS` only immediately
   523	before a CALL-family opcode.

   525	## Daybreak re-review #4 — SP-R4
   526	
   527	### BLS slash surface and reservation race (SP-R4-H-01)
   528	
   529	`executeSlashWithBLSAfterReleasing` has been removed from SP, its admin-call shim, ABI and tests.
   530	The sole BLS penalty route is `executeSlashWithBLS`, which reverts
   531	`SlashBlockedByInflight(reserved)` while any counted reservation is live. Any address may first call
   532	`releaseStaleSponsorship(opHash)`. This is intentionally not atomic with the BLS slash: a colluding
   533	operator can delay a BLS slash by creating a new stale record before each attempt, but each delay
   534	attempt costs a UserOperation whose `postOp` must fail. The owner route
   535	`slashOperatorAfterReleasing` remains atomic and is `onlyOwner`; tests prove both the configured
   536	`BLS_AGGREGATOR` and an arbitrary non-owner are rejected.
   537	
   538	The exact source-derived SP/SPAdmin selector set whose access decision admits `BLS_AGGREGATOR` is:
   539	
   540	- `0xad1c98d7` — `queueSlash(address)`
   541	- `0x53afb8be` — `updatePriceDVT(int256,uint256,bytes,uint8)`
   542	- `0x079d2d42` — `executeSlashWithBLS(address,uint8,bytes)`
   543	
   544	`SuperPaymasterBLSSelectorSurface.t.sol` parses both `SuperPaymaster.sol` and
   545	`SuperPaymasterAdmin.sol`, enumerates every function body that combines `msg.sender` with
   546	`BLS_AGGREGATOR`, and asserts that this is the complete set.
   547	The integrated tree must compare the BLSAggregator generic-path denylist against these three
   548	selectors; that denylist is owned by the BLS worktree.
   549	
   550	### Deployed storage baseline and no legacy inflight state (SP-R4-H-02 / M-02)
   551	
   552	The live Sepolia implementation is SuperPaymaster 5.4.2. The deployed tag evidence is
   553	`git show v5.4.2:storage-layout/SuperPaymaster.json`: `_blsSlashCdFloor` is slot 36 and
   554	`uint256[28] __gap` begins at slot 37. There is no `_inflight` mapping in that layout. OP is a fresh
   555	deployment. Therefore no target chain can contain a pre-5.5.1 `_inflight` record, and
   556	`inflightReserved == 0` genuinely means no reservation on both targets.
   557	
   558	The defensive 5.5.0 context/record decoder branches remain because removing them would add churn
   559	across settlement compatibility code without improving target-chain safety. They are unreachable on
   560	the target chains. In particular, target-chain `Inflight.counted` is always written `true`; a false
   561	value can arise only on a non-target fork that actually ran the unreleased 5.5.0 shape.
   562	
   563	The layout gate now pins that exact v5.4.2 snapshot (SHA-256
   564	`ac3d211c58b59bd03cb4fb23e52b3dccd25de75b1b00fc9b612affd13d905d87`) and allowlists exactly:
   565	slot 37 `_inflight` (including appended member `Inflight.counted`), slot 38 `_gasParams`, slot 39
   566	`_pendingGasParams`, slot 40 `guardian`/`paused`, slot 41 `pendingWithdrawals`, slot 42
   567	`slashQueues`, and slot 43 `inflightReserved`. The gap shrinks to `uint256[21]` at slot 44, so its
   568	end remains slot 65. Scope aliases normalize only `SuperPaymasterStorage` to the old
   569	`SuperPaymaster` declaring name. The self-test mutates a struct member and removes
   570	`Inflight.counted`; both mutations are rejected.

   572	### Amsterdam gas floors (SP-c)
   573	
   574	Governance floors now equal the release tuple `(MIN, SETTLE, C_WRAP, C_POSTOP) = (500k, 450k, 5k, 450k)`.
   575	The old gasleft-delta metric under-counted EIP-8037: bisected real-handleOps requirements are
   576	BALANCE 375,528 and CREDIT 379,828, so `ceil(W x 1.15) = 436,803`; the old floor tuple is rejected.
   577	The release tuple settles on Amsterdam with 30,651 headroom (469,349 required vs 500,000).
   578	MIN must also cover `SETTLE + floor(SETTLE / 63) + 20,000`: EIP-150 retained gas plus ~12.2k call overhead and ~7.8k margin.
   579	The release spacing is 477,142, below the unchanged 500,000 absolute floor; the old 620k/600k tuple is rejected.
   580	Real-EntryPoint BALANCE/CREDIT tests validate the exact governance minimum at SETTLE 450k, 600k and 1M.
   581	Zero-slot defaults changed with the floors: MIN 200k -> 500k, SETTLE 160k -> 450k, C_POSTOP 180k -> 450k
   582	(C_WRAP stays 5k). An all-zero slot therefore behaves exactly like the release tuple; the manifest still
   583	writes the tuple explicitly. LEGACY constants are unchanged.
   584	
   585	`LEGACY_SETTLE_GAS_BOUND = 160k` and `LEGACY_C_WRAP_GAS = 30k` are unchanged. They apply only to an
   586	unreleased 5.5.0 352-byte context that could survive only within one `handleOps` transaction.
   587	Sepolia upgrades from 5.4.2, whose tag source emits a 160-byte context, so that legacy path is
   588	unreachable across the 5.4.2 -> 5.5.1 upgrade. The executor's own minimum still admits 480k; that is
   589	raised to 500k in the separate manifest PR under `script/upgrade`. A release run before that PR lands
   590	would queue a tuple the contract rejects (`InvalidConfiguration` at queue), so that PR is a release
   591	prerequisite, not a follow-up.
   592	
   593	Migration and integrator notes (release procedure):
   594	- `_gpRaw` substitutes the defaults only for an all-zero slot. A proxy that already stores a tuple
   595	  keeps it until governance queues a new one (48 h timelock). Sepolia's 5.4.2 proxy has a zero slot, so
   596	  it gets the release values on upgrade; any other proxy must be read first.
   597	- Floors are checked at queue and at execute, so a pending tuple below the new floors can no longer be
   598	  executed after the upgrade: cancel it and re-queue a valid one.
   599	- UserOps with `paymasterPostOpGasLimit < 500000` are rejected at validation. SDK/bundler integrators
   600	  must send at least 500,000.

   660	The slash base deliberately excludes uncounted reservations created with the pre-5.5.1 `Inflight`

   662	cannot be included safely without an explicit migration. This state is unreachable on every release
   663	target: live Sepolia runs `SuperPaymaster-5.4.2`, whose storage layout has no `_inflight` mapping, and
   664	OP is a fresh deployment. The upgrade manifest must assert, before execution, that the observed FROM
   665	version is exactly `SuperPaymaster-5.4.2`; this is a manifest requirement, not an operator assumption.
   666	An upgrade from any other FROM version is outside this release's proven state set and must stop.

   737	## Re-review #619 B1
   738	
   739	Operator withdrawals now use exact escrow plus a bounded execution window. `requestWithdraw(amount)`
   740	immediately moves `amount` from the operator's sponsorship balance into the existing
   741	`PendingWithdrawal.amount` field. The request matures after the 48-hour delay and can execute only
   742	during `[readyAt, readyAt + 24 hours]`. Cancellation returns the escrow to sponsorship at any time;
   743	after the window, anyone may call `expireWithdraw(operator)` to do the same. Only an actual
   744	withdrawal reduces `totalTrackedBalance`.
   745	
   746	Escrow is excluded from new sponsorship but remains slashable. Slashing computes its 30% cap over
   747	the operator's unescrowed balance plus withdrawal escrow, consumes the unescrowed balance first,
   748	and then reduces the escrow. `SuperPaymasterLens.dryRunValidation` requires no code change: it
   749	already reads only `aPNTsBalance`, so escrow is excluded automatically in the same way as production
   750	validation.
   751	
   752	Accepted residual: during `[readyAt, readyAt + W]`, where `W = 24 hours`, escrowed funds can leave
   753	without further notice. Inside that window the escrowed slice can escape the slash entirely: a
   754	slash that lands after the withdrawal executes finds nothing left of it. Those funds did not
   755	sponsor operations while escrowed, and the request gave at least 48 hours of public notice
   756	(`OperatorWithdrawalRequested` carries `readyAt` and `expiresAt`), so the exposure is limited to
   757	the escrowed slice during at most `W` per request cycle.
   758	
   759	Side effect: `xPNTsTokenV2Ext` uses `operators(community).aPNTsBalance` as the backing for the
   760	community-token issuance ceiling. Because escrow leaves `aPNTsBalance` at request time, the backing
   761	(and so the ceiling) drops when a withdrawal is requested, not when it executes. That is the
   762	conservative direction; `isOverIssued()` can turn true up to 48 hours earlier than before.
   763	
   764	Deposit cap: a deposit reverts `AmountExceedsUint128` unless the liquid balance, the withdrawal
   765	escrow, the in-flight reservation and the deposit together fit `uint128`. Every later credit back
   766	into `aPNTsBalance` (escrow cancel/expire, postOp refund, stale release) therefore cannot overflow.
   767	Tests: `test_B1_deposit_cap_counts_withdrawal_escrow`,
   768	`test_B1_deposit_cap_counts_inflight_reservation_then_stale_release_and_slash`, and
   769	`test_B1_expireWithdraw_at_exactly_expiry_reverts_and_one_second_later_succeeds`; each is red
   770	against its mutant (escrow ignored, reservation ignored, `<=` relaxed to `<`).

   777	tests, including the M1 replay regression, intentionally skip on Cancun; Prague

   779	tests using AnchoredOverIssueFraudProofVerifier are **local adapter** evidence,

   784	### M1 execution floor and disclosed residuals (2026-11-13)
   785	
   786	`BLSAggregator.verifyAndExecute` rejects `proposalId < proposalFloor` with
   787	`InvalidProposalId` only when `msg.sender == DVT_VALIDATOR`. M1 covers slash and
   788	aggregator-routed reputation proposals executed through the current DVT, where
   789	IDs are DVT-allocated. An allocated id with a ready proof becomes stale on that
   790	path when a later rotation raises the floor; reactivating its original DVT does
   791	not restore it. A newly allocated id at or above the fresh floor remains
   792	executable with its own valid proof. Every caller, including the owner, still
   793	receives `InvalidProposalId` for zero or an id at or above `2^128`. The monotonic
   794	floor preserves the exhausted value `2^128` across rotations.
   795	
   796	The accepted, disclosed residuals are:
   797	
   798	- Owner-direct `verifyAndExecute` accepts caller-chosen ids below the floor.
   799	  This is the documented owner-mediated residual: rotation does not revoke that
   800	  route's unused signed authorizations. Signature, replay and DVT callback checks
   801	  still apply; the floor must not treat an owner-chosen id as a DVT allocation.
   802	- Unused pre-rotation generic proposals remain owner/DVT-executable through
   803	  `executeProposal`; their typed replay keys are separate from the raw-id floor.
   804	- Pre-rotation reputation proofs can still reach Registry through an authorized
   805	  reputation source. That route remains source-gated, enforces per-user epoch
   806	  progression and bounds score changes to ±100. It does not inherit the
   807	  aggregator's execution floor.
   808	- An unused pre-rotation consensus queue proof can still set a reversible
   809	  pre-flag. A BLS-queued freeze has **no time expiry**:
   810	  `SuperPaymasterStorage._isSlashPending` expires only a guardian queue after
   811	  `GUARDIAN_SLASH_FREEZE`. The owner can always cancel the flag with
   812	  `SuperPaymasterAdmin.cancelSlash`. `usedSlashQueueHashes` makes the proof
   813	  one-shot per `(operator, level, epoch)`, even after cancellation. The pre-flag
   814	  moves no funds: execution through the current DVT requires a separate fresh
   815	  slash proof with an id at or above the current floor. Relabelling an old proof
   816	  with a fresh id also fails signature verification. Owner-direct execution with
   817	  caller-chosen ids remains the residual described above. The independent owner
   818	  slash authority is unchanged.
   819	
   820	`RotationFloorExecution.t.sol` covers stale current-DVT execution after reactivation,
   821	fresh execution, later rotation invalidation, stale queue versus DVT fund-moving execution,
   822	exact namespace exhaustion, suspended key ownership and the disclosed queue
   823	residual. Signature-dependent tests execute with genuine Prague precompiles and
   824	skip on Cancun. `test_RotationAllocationFloorPreservesAuthorizedRegistryProof`
   825	also checks that the same stale reputation proof fails through the reactivated DVT
   826	before succeeding through the authorized Registry source. The same real-Registry
   827	suite adds `test_PostRotationDvtReputationUpdateExecutes` and
   828	`test_OwnerDirectLowIdStillExecutesAfterRotation`, proving successful reputation
   829	updates with genuine signatures on both authorized routes. Final suite counts,
   830	runtime size and changed files are recorded in `.rv-narrow.md`; ABI/docs
   831	regeneration is left to the calling session.

   833	## Generic-path selector gaps and the staking slasher role (2026-11-15)
   834	
   835	BLSAggregator-4.14.0 as merged in #630 had two gaps on the GENERIC `executeProposal` path
   836	(caller-chosen threshold >= `minThreshold`, no `proposalFloor`). Both are closed here.
   837	
   838	1. **`Registry.batchUpdateGlobalReputation` was not blocked.** Registry re-verifies the proof
   839	   itself, but under `blsDomainSeparator() = keccak(DOMAIN_NAME, chainid, blsAggregator, Registry)`.
   840	   That domain does not change on a DVT rotation, and Registry has no floor. A reputation proof
   841	   signed before a rotation and never executed could therefore still execute through a generic call,
   842	   bypassing the M1 floor guarantee.
   843	   - The #630 review recorded this path only as "consumes a raw id". The floor bypass was found
   844	     afterwards.
   845	   - Test: `test_PreRotationReputationProofCannotExecuteThroughGenericPath` (Prague, genuine keys).
   846	     Removing the block turns it red.
   847	2. **`GTokenStaking.slash` and `slashByDVT` were not blocked.** `DeployLive` made the aggregator an
   848	   authorized slasher, so a `minThreshold` quorum could slash any stake by any amount. This bypassed
   849	   severity bps, cooldown and the floor.
   850	   - The live Sepolia 4.11.0 aggregator has the same gap, with `minThreshold` 2. Only its owner (the
   851	     deployer EOA) can call `executeProposal` there.
   852	
   853	**Fixes**
   854	- The H-1 denylist now also blocks `batchUpdateGlobalReputation`, `slash` and `slashByDVT`.
   855	  BLSAggregator is 24,529 B (47 B headroom). Per-selector blocking is close to full: 5.5.x should
   856	  move to a per-target allowlist, or move the gates into the callees.
   857	- Versions are BLSAggregator-4.14.1 and DVTValidator-0.8.1. The 4.14.0 / 0.8.0 merged in #630
   858	  carries the gaps above.
   859	- `scripts/check_generic_selector_coverage.py` (CI, every PR) enumerates every non-view function in
   860	  the SuperPaymaster, Registry, GTokenStaking and DVTValidator ABIs. Each function whose code
   861	  references an aggregator identity must be classified as blocked or allowed-with-reason.
   862	- **No slasher role in 5.5.0.** The aggregator's only stake slash is `executeGuardianSlash`, which
   863	  cannot be reached while `fraudProofVerifier == 0`. `DeployLive` / `DeployAnvil` no longer grant the
   864	  role and assert it is absent.
   865	  - Enabling guardian slash later grants the role in the same timelock batch as
   866	    `proposeFraudProofVerifier`.
   867	  - Before enabling, see YetAnotherAA-Validator#441: the verifier must recompute the 4.14.0 signers
   868	    commitment, which includes `blockhash(block.number-1)`.
   869	- **Review L1.** Owner-forwarded `DVTValidator.registerBLSPublicKey` now requires
   870	  `aggregator.owner() == msg.sender`, as `removeValidator` already did.
   871	  - Test: `test_RegisterBLSPublicKey_OwnerDivergenceClosesOwnerPath`.
   872	
   873	**Disclosed residuals**
   874	- `Registry.updateOperatorBlacklist` stays generic-callable. A pre-rotation proof for the next unused
   875	  `blacklistNonce` remains valid. Its effect is limited to blocking or unblocking users; it moves no
   876	  funds.
   877	- `SP.updatePriceDVT` stays generic-callable. Each update is limited to +-20% against the SP cache.
   878	  The +-20% Chainlink band applies only while Chainlink is fresh (< 2 h). With a stale feed, cumulative
   879	  drift is bounded only by `[MIN, MAX]_ETH_USD_PRICE`, freshness and increasing `updatedAt`.
   880	- `ReputationSystem.setCommunityReputation` stays generic-callable (#631 review L1). It is open to
   881	  any Registry reputation source, and the aggregator is one on both chains. The current quorum can
   882	  therefore write any community score at `minThreshold`, with no proof.
   883	  - `communityReputations` has no reader in `contracts/src`. The coverage script fails if one is
   884	    added; that is the reopen condition.
   885	  - The SDK exposes the value only as a raw getter, documented as unused by the protocol.
   886	- The generic path can call `transfer` / `approve` on any token the aggregator holds. The aggregator
   887	  must hold no assets; step 13 reads its GToken, aPNTs, xPNTs and ETH balances back as 0.
   888	- Every "onlyOwner; the aggregator is not the owner" allowance holds only while the aggregator owns
   889	  nothing and holds no role. This is enforced by the coverage script's deploy-path ownership check
   890	  and by the step-13 readbacks OWNER-NOT-AGGREGATOR and AGG-NOT-DVT-VALIDATOR.

    11	/**
    12	 * @title SuperPaymasterStorage
    13	 * @notice D5b: the ONE storage/inheritance chain shared by the SuperPaymaster core and its
    14	 *         SuperPaymasterAdmin extension (reached from the core's fallback via DELEGATECALL).
    15	 * @dev    Both contracts inherit exactly this chain — BasePaymasterUpgradeable(Ownable2StepNamespaced
    16	 *         → Ownable, Initializable, UUPSUpgradeable) + ReentrancyGuard + the state below — so they
    17	 *         agree on every slot by construction; scripts/check-sp-layout.py re-checks it on the
    18	 *         compiled artifacts. The deployed 5.4.2 baseline ends at `_blsSlashCdFloor` in slot 36
    19	 *         and has its gap at slots 37..64. The 5.5.x layout uses exactly slots 37 `_inflight`,
    20	 *         38 `_gasParams`, 39 `_pendingGasParams`, 40 `guardian` + `paused`, 41
    21	 *         `pendingWithdrawals`, 42 `slashQueues`, and 43 `inflightReserved`; the remaining gap
    22	 *         starts at slot 44 and preserves the old end slot. scripts/check_storage_layout.py allows
    23	 *         only those listed appends against the deployed baseline.
    24	 *
    25	 *         RULES
    26	 *         - Declaration ORDER below is the storage order. Never insert, reorder or resize; append
    27	 *           only before `__gap` and shrink the gap by the same number of slots.
    28	 *         - Any override that changes a BASE contract's behaviour (transferOwnership, …) belongs in
    29	 *           this chain or in the core, never only in the extension: a selector the core has is
    30	 *           always answered by the core (D5b-design §2.1).
    31	 *         - Immutables live in the bytecode of each contract: the core and the extension are
    32	 *           constructed with the same (entryPoint, REGISTRY, ETH_USD_PRICE_FEED) — the core creates
    33	 *           its extension in its own constructor (D5b-design §2.2).
    34	 */
    35	abstract contract SuperPaymasterStorage is BasePaymasterUpgradeable, ReentrancyGuard {

   387	    /// @dev Reverts unless `account` has the role and its live stake meets the current minimum.
   388	    function _requireSuperOperatorRoleFor(address account) internal view {
   389	        if (!_hasEffectiveSuperStake(account)) revert Unauthorized();
   390	    }
   391	
   392	    function _hasEffectiveSuperStake(address account) internal view returns (bool) {
   393	        if (!REGISTRY.hasRole(ROLE_PAYMASTER_SUPER, account)) return false;
   394	        IRegistry.RoleConfig memory config = REGISTRY.getRoleConfig(ROLE_PAYMASTER_SUPER);
   395	        return REGISTRY.getEffectiveStake(account, ROLE_PAYMASTER_SUPER) >= config.minStake;
   396	    }
   397	
   398	    /// @dev The only deletion path for an in-flight record. Only 5.5.1 records entered the aggregate.
   399	    function _clearInflight(bytes32 opHash) internal {
   400	        Inflight memory f = _inflight[opHash];
   401	        if (f.operator == address(0)) return;
   402	        if (f.counted) inflightReserved[f.operator] -= f.a0;
   403	        delete _inflight[opHash];
   404	    }
   405	
   406	    function _inflightSlot(bytes32 opHash) private pure returns (bytes32) {
   407	        return keccak256(abi.encode(opHash, INFLIGHT_SEED));
   408	    }
   409	
   410	    function _setInflightLive(bytes32 opHash, bool on) internal {
   411	        bytes32 slot = _inflightSlot(opHash);
   412	        uint256 v = on ? 1 : 0;
   413	        assembly { tstore(slot, v) }
   414	    }
   415	
   416	    function _isInflightLive(bytes32 opHash) private view returns (bool live) {
   417	        bytes32 slot = _inflightSlot(opHash);
   418	        assembly { live := tload(slot) }
   419	    }
   420	
   421	    function _releaseStaleSponsorship(bytes32 opHash) internal {
   422	        Inflight memory f = _inflight[opHash];
   423	        if (f.operator == address(0)) return;
   424	        if (_isInflightLive(opHash)) revert SponsorshipInFlight();
   425	        _clearInflight(opHash);
   426	        operators[f.operator].aPNTsBalance += uint128(f.a0);
   427	        emit SponsorshipReleased(opHash, f.operator, f.a0);
   428	    }
   429	
   430	    /// @dev Legacy flags remain effective. Only an unconfirmed guardian queue expires.
   431	    function _isSlashPending(address operator) internal view returns (bool) {
   432	        if (!_pendingSlash[operator]) return false;
   433	        SlashQueue memory q = slashQueues[operator];
   434	        return !q.guardianQueued || block.timestamp < uint256(q.queuedAt) + GUARDIAN_SLASH_FREEZE;
   435	    }
   436	
   437	    function _clearSlashQueue(address operator) internal {
   438	        _pendingSlash[operator] = false;
   439	        delete slashQueues[operator];
   440	    }
   441	
   442	    /// @dev The GasParams slot as one word (minPostOpGas | settle << 32 | cWrap << 64 | cPostop << 96);
   443	    ///      an all-zero slot (never set / pre-Part-B proxy) = the defaults.
   444	    function _gpRaw() internal view returns (uint256 raw) {
   445	        assembly ("memory-safe") { raw := sload(_gasParams.slot) }
   446	        if (raw == 0) {
   447	            raw = MIN_POST_OP_GAS | (SETTLE_GAS_BOUND << 32) | (C_WRAP_GAS << 64) | (C_POSTOP_GAS << 96);
   448	        }
   449	    }
   450	}

    15	/**
    16	 * @title SuperPaymaster (CORE)
    17	 * @notice SuperPaymaster - Unified Registry based Multi-Operator Paymaster
    18	 * @dev    D5b split (D5b-design §2): this CORE holds every ERC-4337 hot path — validatePaymasterUserOp,
    19	 *         postOp, the reservation (`_reserveForOp`, `_tokenWord`), `releaseStaleSponsorship`,
    20	 *         `inflightOf` — plus operator deposit / withdraw, EntryPoint deposit / stake, UUPS
    21	 *         (`upgradeToAndCall`, `proxiableUUID`, `_authorizeUpgrade`) and the GOV-2 two-step ownership
    22	 *         overrides (inherited from Ownable2StepNamespaced). Governance, administration and
    23	 *         non-hot-path views are served by `EXTENSION` (SuperPaymasterAdmin) through `fallback()`
    24	 *         (DELEGATECALL: shared storage, msg.sender / msg.value / event emitter stay the proxy's).
    25	 *         Validation and postOp never cross the fallback, so ERC-7562 behaviour is unchanged.
    26	 *
    27	 *         The extension is created in this constructor with the SAME immutables, and is replaced
    28	 *         together with the implementation on every upgrade. It is non-upgradeable, has no
    29	 *         initializer, and calling it directly only touches its own unused storage.
    30	 *
    31	 *         SDK: calls go to one address; use the merged ABI `abis/SuperPaymaster.full.json`.
    32	 */
    33	contract SuperPaymaster is SuperPaymasterStorage, IVersioned {
    34	    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;
    35	
    36	    /// @notice Administration / governance / views implementation (SuperPaymasterAdmin).
    37	    address public immutable EXTENSION;
    38	
    39	    /// @dev 5.5.0 postOp context (spec §3.2, R10-M3: price snapshot taken at validation).
    40	    struct OpCtx {
    41	        address token;
    42	        address user;
    43	        uint256 a0;
    44	        bytes32 opHash;
    45	        address operator;
    46	        uint8 mode;
    47	        uint128 callGas;
    48	        uint128 postOpGas;
    49	        int256 price;
    50	        uint8 decimals;
    51	        uint256 aPriceUSD;
    52	    }
    53	
    54	    // Context format (Part B, Codex rounds 1-3). OpCtx is an upgrade-compatibility surface in
    55	    // BOTH directions; every word of OpCtx stays ABI-canonical for its 5.5.0 type (never pack into
    56	    // a narrow-typed word: 5.5.0's decoder reverts on dirty bits).
    57	    //   emitted : abi.encode(OpCtx) (the 11 5.5.0 words, 352 B) ‖ one trailing word (384 B total):
    58	    //             the GasParams slot as validation saw it (minPostOpGas | settleGasBound << 32 |
    59	    //             cWrap << 64 | cPostop << 96; never zero — defaults substituted) in bits 0-127, and
    60	    //             (protocolFeeBPS + 1) << 128 in bits 128-255 (0 there = no fee snapshot).
    61	    //             5.5.0's `abi.decode(context, (OpCtx))` ignores the trailing word, and every earlier
    62	    //             reader of word 12 takes uint32 slices below bit 128, so the fee bits are invisible
    63	    //             to a rolled-back implementation (it charges at the live fee, as it always did).
    64	    //   accepted: 384 B → snapshot; 352 B (a 5.5.0 context, forward upgrade) → LEGACY rules;
    65	    //             word 12 is read ONLY when the length is exactly 384; a 384 B context whose fee bits
    66	    //             are 0 (emitted before the fee snapshot existed) is charged at the live fee.
    67	    /// @dev Emit-only layout: OpCtx's 11 words + the trailing snapshot word.
    68	    struct OpCtxOut {
    69	        address token;
    70	        address user;
    71	        uint256 a0;
    72	        bytes32 opHash;
    73	        address operator;
    74	        uint8 mode;
    75	        uint128 callGas;
    76	        uint128 postOpGas;
    77	        int256 price;
    78	        uint8 decimals;
    79	        uint256 aPriceUSD;
    80	        uint256 gasSnap;
    81	    }
    82	    uint256 internal constant CTX_LEN = 384;
    83	    uint256 internal constant FEE_SNAP_SHIFT = 128;
    84	    /// @dev 5.5.0 values, applied ONLY to its 352-byte context. Such a context can exist only inside
    85	    ///      one handleOps transaction, and 5.5.0 was never deployed. Sepolia upgrades from 5.4.2,
    86	    ///      whose context is 160 bytes, so this path is unreachable across the 5.4.2 -> 5.5.1 upgrade.
    87	    uint256 internal constant LEGACY_SETTLE_GAS_BOUND = 160_000;
    88	    uint256 internal constant LEGACY_C_WRAP_GAS = 30_000;
    89	
    90	    function version() external pure virtual override returns (string memory) {
    91	        return "SuperPaymaster-5.5.2";
    92	    }
    93	
    94	    // ====================================
    95	    // Constructor & Initializer (UUPS)
    96	    // ====================================
    97	
    98	    /// @custom:oz-upgrades-unsafe-allow constructor
    99	    constructor(IEntryPoint _entryPoint, IRegistry _registry, address _ethUsdPriceFeed)
   100	        SuperPaymasterStorage(_entryPoint, _registry, _ethUsdPriceFeed)
   101	    {
   102	        // D5b-design §2.2: the extension mirrors this implementation's immutables by construction.
   103	        EXTENSION = address(new SuperPaymasterAdmin(_entryPoint, _registry, _ethUsdPriceFeed));
   104	    }
   105	
   106	    /**
   107	     * @notice Initialize the UUPS proxy state
   108	     * @param _owner Contract owner
   109	     * @param _apntsToken aPNTs token address
   110	     * @param _protocolTreasury Treasury address for protocol fees
   111	     * @param _priceStalenessThreshold Oracle staleness threshold in seconds
   112	     */
   113	    function initialize(
   114	        address _owner,
   115	        address _apntsToken,
   116	        address _protocolTreasury,
   117	        uint256 _priceStalenessThreshold
   118	    ) external initializer {
   119	        if (_owner == address(0)) revert InvalidOwner();
   120	        __BasePaymaster_init(_owner);
   121	        // Note: _apntsToken can be address(0) during staged deployment
   122	        // (deployed later via setAPNTsToken which has its own zero-address check)
   123	        APNTS_TOKEN = _apntsToken;
   124	        treasury = _protocolTreasury != address(0) ? _protocolTreasury : _owner;
   125	        uint256 staleness = _priceStalenessThreshold > 0 ? _priceStalenessThreshold : 3600;
   126	        // Same range as PaymasterBase.setPriceStalenessThreshold. There is no setter here, so this is
   127	        // the only write: an oversized value underflows `block.timestamp - threshold` in updatePrice
   128	        // and truncates `uint48(updatedAt + threshold)` (validUntil).
   129	        if (staleness < 60 || staleness > 86400) revert InvalidConfiguration();
   130	        priceStalenessThreshold = staleness;
   131	        // Default values must be set explicitly (proxy storage doesn't inherit implementation defaults)
   132	        aPNTsPriceUSD = 0.02 ether;
   133	        protocolFeeBPS = 1000;
   134	    }
   135	
   136	    // ====================================
   137	    // Extension routing
   138	    // ====================================
   139	
   140	    /// @dev Every selector this core does not define is executed by EXTENSION against the proxy's
   141	    ///      storage. NON-payable: plain ETH transfers are still rejected (there is no receive()).
   142	    fallback() external {
   143	        address ext = EXTENSION;
   144	        assembly {
   145	            calldatacopy(0, 0, calldatasize())
   146	            let ok := delegatecall(gas(), ext, 0, calldatasize(), 0, 0)
   147	            returndatacopy(0, 0, returndatasize())
   148	            switch ok
   149	            case 0 { revert(0, returndatasize()) }
   150	            default { return(0, returndatasize()) }
   151	        }
   152	    }
   153	
   154	    // ====================================
   155	    // Operator deposits / withdrawals
   156	    // ====================================
   157	
   158	    /// @notice Deposit aPNTs from msg.sender into their own operator balance (pull mode).
   159	    function deposit(uint256 amount) external nonReentrant {
   160	        _requireSuperOperatorRoleFor(msg.sender);
   161	        // This might revert if Token blocks transferFrom (Secure Token)
   162	        IERC20(APNTS_TOKEN).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);
   163	        _creditDeposit(msg.sender, amount);
   164	    }
   165	
   166	    /// @dev Shared deposit accounting: overflow-check, credit operator balance,
   167	    ///      bump totalTrackedBalance, emit. Used by deposit/onTransferReceived/depositFor.
   168	    function _creditDeposit(address operator, uint256 amount) internal {
   169	        // Every later credit back into aPNTsBalance (cancel/expire of escrow, postOp refund or stale
   170	        // release of a reservation) must still fit uint128, so the cap covers all three buckets.
   171	        uint256 collateral = uint256(operators[operator].aPNTsBalance) + pendingWithdrawals[operator].amount
   172	            + inflightReserved[operator];
   173	        if (collateral > type(uint128).max || amount > type(uint128).max - collateral) {
   174	            revert AmountExceedsUint128();
   175	        }
   176	        // forge-lint: disable-next-line(unsafe-typecast)
   177	        operators[operator].aPNTsBalance += uint128(amount);
   178	        totalTrackedBalance += amount;
   179	        emit ISuperPaymaster.OperatorDeposited(operator, amount);
   180	    }
   181	
   182	    /**
   183	     * @notice Handle ERC1363 transferAndCall (Push Mode)
   184	     * @dev Safe deposit mechanism for tokens blocking transferFrom
   185	     */
   186	    function onTransferReceived(address, address from, uint256 value, bytes calldata)
   187	        external
   188	        nonReentrant
   189	        returns (bytes4)
   190	    {
   191	        if (msg.sender != APNTS_TOKEN) revert Unauthorized();
   192	        _requireSuperOperatorRoleFor(from);
   193	        _creditDeposit(from, value);
   194	        return this.onTransferReceived.selector;
   195	    }
   196	
   197	    /// @notice Deposit aPNTs on behalf of a specific operator address (must approve first).
   198	    function depositFor(address targetOperator, uint256 amount) external nonReentrant {
   199	        _requireSuperOperatorRoleFor(targetOperator);
   200	        IERC20(APNTS_TOKEN).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);
   201	        _creditDeposit(targetOperator, amount);
   202	    }
   203	
   204	    /// @notice Escrow operator funds and start the withdrawal delay and execution window.
   205	    function requestWithdraw(uint256 amount) external {
   206	        if (_isSlashPending(msg.sender)) revert SlashPending();
   207	        if (pendingWithdrawals[msg.sender].amount != 0) revert WithdrawalPending();
   208	        uint256 balance = operators[msg.sender].aPNTsBalance;
   209	        if (amount == 0 || balance < amount) revert InsufficientBalance(balance, amount);
   210	        uint48 readyAt = uint48(block.timestamp) + OPERATOR_WITHDRAWAL_DELAY;
   211	        uint48 expiresAt = readyAt + OPERATOR_WITHDRAWAL_WINDOW;
   212	        operators[msg.sender].aPNTsBalance = uint128(balance - amount);
   213	        pendingWithdrawals[msg.sender] = PendingWithdrawal(uint128(amount), readyAt);
   214	        emit OperatorWithdrawalRequested(msg.sender, amount, readyAt, expiresAt);
   215	    }
   216	
   217	    /// @notice Cancel a pending withdrawal request.
   218	    function cancelWithdraw() external {
   219	        uint256 amount = pendingWithdrawals[msg.sender].amount;
   220	        if (amount == 0) revert NoPendingWithdrawal();
   221	        delete pendingWithdrawals[msg.sender];
   222	        operators[msg.sender].aPNTsBalance += uint128(amount);
   223	        emit OperatorWithdrawalCancelled(msg.sender, amount);
   224	    }
   225	
   226	    /// @notice Execute a matured withdrawal request.
   227	    function withdraw(uint256 amount) external nonReentrant {
   228	        if (_isSlashPending(msg.sender)) revert SlashPending();
   229	        PendingWithdrawal storage pending = pendingWithdrawals[msg.sender];
   230	        if (pending.amount == 0) revert NoPendingWithdrawal();
   231	        if (uint48(block.timestamp) < pending.readyAt) revert WithdrawalNotReady(pending.readyAt);
   232	        uint48 expiresAt = pending.readyAt + OPERATOR_WITHDRAWAL_WINDOW;
   233	        if (block.timestamp > expiresAt) revert WithdrawalExpired(expiresAt);
   234	        if (amount == 0 || pending.amount < amount) revert InsufficientBalance(pending.amount, amount);
   235	        pending.amount -= uint128(amount);
   236	        if (pending.amount == 0) delete pendingWithdrawals[msg.sender];
   237	        totalTrackedBalance -= amount;
   238	        IERC20(APNTS_TOKEN).safeTransfer(msg.sender, amount);
   239	        emit ISuperPaymaster.OperatorWithdrawn(msg.sender, amount);
   240	    }
   241	
   242	    // ====================================
   243	    // Paymaster Implementation
   244	    // ====================================
   245	
   246	    function _calculateAPNTsAmount(uint256 ethAmountWei) internal view returns (uint256) {
   247	        PriceCache memory cache = cachedPrice;
   248	        int256 ethUsdPrice = cache.price;
   249	        if (ethUsdPrice <= 0) revert OracleError();
   250	        return Math.mulDiv(
   251	            ethAmountWei * uint256(ethUsdPrice),
   252	            1e18,
   253	            (10 ** uint256(cache.decimals)) * aPNTsPriceUSD,
   254	            Math.Rounding.Ceil
   255	        );
   256	    }
   257	
   258	    function validatePaymasterUserOp(PackedUserOperation calldata userOp, bytes32 userOpHash, uint256 maxCost)
   259	        external
   260	        override
   261	        onlyEntryPoint
   262	        nonReentrant
   263	        returns (bytes memory context, uint256 validationData)
   264	    {
   265	        // 0. GOV-2 global stop: checked BEFORE anything in the op is parsed, so every op —
   266	        //    including a malformed one — gets SIG_FAILURE, never a revert. Reads SP's own slot.
   267	        if (paused) return ("", _packValidationData(true, 0, 0));
   268	
   269	        // 1. Extract Operator
   270	        address operator = _extractOperator(userOp);
   271	
   272	        ISuperPaymaster.OperatorConfig storage config = operators[operator];
   273	
   274	        // 2. Validate Operator Role & Config (Pure Storage)
   275	        // Check 1: Must be Configured (implies registered/valid)
   276	        if (!config.isConfigured) {
   277	            return ("", _packValidationData(true, 0, 0));
   278	        }
   279	
   280	        // Initialize Validation Times
   281	        // V3.6 FIX: Return validUntil to enforce Staleness Check and validAfter for Rate Limit
   282	        uint48 validUntil = uint48(cachedPrice.updatedAt + priceStalenessThreshold);
   283	        uint48 validAfter = 0;
   284	
   285	        // Check 2: Must not be Paused
   286	        if (config.isPaused) {
   287	            return ("", _packValidationData(true, 0, 0));
   288	        }
   289	
   290	        // V5.3: Dual-channel identity check (SBT holder OR ERC-8004 Agent NFT)
   291	        if (!isEligibleForSponsorship(userOp.sender)) {
   292	            return ("", _packValidationData(true, 0, 0));
   293	        }
   294	
   295	        // C-04: reject a paymasterPostOpGasLimit too low for postOp to complete.
   296	        // Without this an attacker forces postOp OOG and the optimistic operator
   297	        // debit (below) is never refunded → operator drain + revenue inflation.
   298	        // GOV-5: one SLOAD of SP's own slot (staked, STO-031); snapshotted into the context.
   299	        uint256 gpRaw = _gpRaw();
   300	        if (userOp.paymasterAndData.length >= POSTOP_GAS_OFFSET + 16) {
   301	            uint128 pmPostOpGas = uint128(bytes16(userOp.paymasterAndData[POSTOP_GAS_OFFSET:POSTOP_GAS_OFFSET + 16]));
   302	            if (pmPostOpGas < uint32(gpRaw)) {
   303	                return ("", _packValidationData(true, 0, 0));
   304	            }
   305	        }
   306	
   307	        // V3.2 Security: Check Blocklist & Rate Limit
   308	        // CONSOLIDATED SLOAD: Get user state (Block status + Timestamp)
   309	        UserOperatorState memory userState = userOpState[operator][userOp.sender];
   310	
   311	        if (userState.isBlocked) {
   312	            return ("", _packValidationData(true, 0, 0));
   313	        }
   314	
   315	        // V3.4: Rate Limiting (Using same SLOAD data)
   316	        if (config.minTxInterval > 0) {
   317	            uint48 lastTime = userState.lastTimestamp;
   318	            // V3.6 FIX: Use validAfter to enforce rate limit instead of reverting on block.timestamp
   319	            if (lastTime != 0) {
   320	                validAfter = lastTime + config.minTxInterval;
   321	            }
   322	        }
   323	
   324	        // 2.1 Token binding + rate commitment (R4-H1; rug-pull protection)
   325	        bytes calldata pmd = userOp.paymasterAndData;
   326	        if (pmd.length < TOKEN_OFFSET + 20) return ("", _packValidationData(true, 0, 0));
   327	        address token = address(bytes20(pmd[TOKEN_OFFSET:TOKEN_OFFSET + 20]));
   328	        if (token != config.xPNTsToken) return ("", _packValidationData(true, 0, 0));
   329	        uint8 flags = pmd.length > FLAGS_OFFSET ? uint8(pmd[FLAGS_OFFSET]) : 0;
   330	        if (flags & (FLAG_SP_RENEW | FLAG_ACCOUNT_RENEW) == (FLAG_SP_RENEW | FLAG_ACCOUNT_RENEW)) {
   331	            return ("", _packValidationData(true, 0, 0));
   332	        }
   333	        uint256 maxRate = abi.decode(pmd[RATE_OFFSET:RATE_OFFSET + 32], (uint256));
   334	        // §3.3: every token call fails CLOSED → sigFail (AA34), never a validation revert (AA33)
   335	        (bool rateOk, uint256 rate) = _tokenWord(token, abi.encodeCall(IxPNTsTokenV2.exchangeRate, ()), true, 32);
   336	        if (!rateOk || rate > maxRate) return ("", _packValidationData(true, 0, 0));
   337	
   338	        // 3. Reservation a0 (spec §10.3): full maxCost at the cached price, + fee + validation buffer
   339	        uint256 aPNTsAmount = _calculateAPNTsAmount(maxCost);
   340	        // The fee a0 was quoted at is also the fee postOp charges (snapshotted into word 12), so a
   341	        // setProtocolFee landing mid-bundle cannot re-price an already-admitted op.
   342	        uint256 feeBps = protocolFeeBPS;
   343	        uint256 totalRate = BPS_DENOMINATOR + feeBps + VALIDATION_BUFFER_BPS;
   344	        aPNTsAmount = Math.mulDiv(aPNTsAmount, totalRate, BPS_DENOMINATOR, Math.Rounding.Ceil);
   345	        // Inflight.a0 is uint96; reject before any token reservation or business-state write.
   346	        if (aPNTsAmount > type(uint96).max) {
   347	            return ("", _packValidationData(true, 0, 0));
   348	        }
   349	
   350	        // 4. Operator solvency — checked BEFORE touching the token
   351	        if (uint256(config.aPNTsBalance) < aPNTsAmount) {
   352	            return ("", _packValidationData(true, 0, 0));
   353	        }
   354	
   355	        // 5. User side: escrow first, credit only on INSUFFICIENT (R-2)
   356	        uint8 mode = _reserveForOp(token, userOp.sender, userOpHash, aPNTsAmount, flags & FLAG_SP_RENEW != 0);
   357	        if (mode == MODE_NONE) return ("", _packValidationData(true, 0, 0));
   358	
   359	        // 6. Operator side: a0 is IN FLIGHT, not revenue, until postOp settles (R10-M1b)
   360	        config.aPNTsBalance -= uint128(aPNTsAmount); // Safe cast due to check above
   361	        config.totalSpent += aPNTsAmount;
   362	        inflightReserved[operator] += aPNTsAmount;
   363	        _inflight[userOpHash] = Inflight(operator, uint96(aPNTsAmount), true);
   364	        _setInflightLive(userOpHash, true);
   365	
   366	        PriceCache memory pc = cachedPrice;
   367	        context = abi.encode(
   368	            OpCtxOut({
   369	                token: token,
   370	                user: userOp.sender,
   371	                a0: aPNTsAmount,
   372	                opHash: userOpHash,
   373	                operator: operator,
   374	                mode: mode,
   375	                callGas: uint128(uint256(userOp.accountGasLimits)),
   376	                postOpGas: uint128(bytes16(pmd[POSTOP_GAS_OFFSET:POSTOP_GAS_OFFSET + 16])),
   377	                price: pc.price,
   378	                decimals: pc.decimals,
   379	                aPriceUSD: aPNTsPriceUSD,
   380	                gasSnap: gpRaw | ((feeBps + 1) << FEE_SNAP_SHIFT)
   381	            })
   382	        );
   383	        return (context, _packValidationData(false, validUntil, validAfter));
   384	    }
   385	
   386	    /// @dev Escrow-then-credit decision (spec §1). Any token failure → no sponsorship (H3-1).
   387	    function _reserveForOp(address token, address user, bytes32 opHash, uint256 a0, bool spRenew)
   388	        internal
   389	        returns (uint8)
   390	    {
   391	        (bool ok, uint256 r) = _tokenWord(
   392	            token, abi.encodeCall(IxPNTsTokenV2.tryLockForGas, (user, opHash, a0, spRenew)), false, 64
   393	        );
   394	        if (!ok) return MODE_NONE;
   395	        if (r == uint256(IxPNTsTokenV2.LockResult.OK)) return MODE_BALANCE;
   396	        if (r != uint256(IxPNTsTokenV2.LockResult.INSUFFICIENT)) return MODE_NONE;
   397	        (ok, r) = _tokenWord(token, abi.encodeCall(IxPNTsTokenV2.tryReserveCredit, (user, opHash, a0)), false, 32);
   398	        return ok && r == uint256(IxPNTsTokenV2.CreditResult.OK) ? MODE_CREDIT : MODE_NONE;
   399	    }
   400	
   401	    /// @dev Validation-time token call that can only fail CLOSED (§3.3, Codex D3): a revert, a
   402	    ///      return shorter than the function's full ABI return (`minLen`: 64 for tryLockForGas's
   403	    ///      two words, 32 otherwise), or any out-of-range first word is reported as `ok = false`
   404	    ///      or a value the caller rejects — never a revert in SP. Copies at most 32 bytes of
   405	    ///      return data (no return-bomb). A typed `try … returns (…)` would still revert on
   406	    ///      malformed success data, because its decoding happens in the caller outside the catch.
   407	    function _tokenWord(address token, bytes memory data, bool isStatic, uint256 minLen)
   408	        private
   409	        returns (bool ok, uint256 w)
   410	    {
   411	        assembly ("memory-safe") {
   412	            switch isStatic
   413	            case 1 { ok := staticcall(gas(), token, add(data, 32), mload(data), 0, 32) }
   414	            default { ok := call(gas(), token, 0, add(data, 32), mload(data), 0, 32) }
   415	            if lt(returndatasize(), minLen) { ok := 0 }
   416	            w := mload(0)
   417	        }
   418	    }
   419	
   420	    // dryRunValidation moved to SuperPaymasterLens in 5.5.0 (spec F1 / §5: EIP-170 headroom).
   421	
   422	    function postOp(PostOpMode, bytes calldata context, uint256 actualGasCost, uint256 actualUserOpFeePerGas)
   423	        external
   424	        override
   425	        onlyEntryPoint
   426	        nonReentrant
   427	    {
   428	        // GOV-2: deliberately NO `paused` check — an op that was validated settles (or is released)
   429	        // normally even if sponsorship is stopped afterwards.
   430	        if (context.length == 0) return;
   431	        // Codex whole-branch review (block 1, informational): abi.decode below tolerates any
   432	        // length >= 352 and silently treats everything except exactly 384 as the legacy (352 B,
   433	        // no gas-param snapshot) format — including malformed lengths that were never actually
   434	        // emitted by _reserveForOp. This implementation's only encode site (OpCtxOut) always emits
   435	        // 384; 352 can only be a context left mid-bundle by the prior 5.5.0 implementation across
   436	        // an upgrade. Any other length is definitionally corrupt; reject it explicitly rather than
   437	        // silently decoding it under legacy rules.
   438	        if (context.length != 352 && context.length != CTX_LEN) revert InvalidContextLength();
   439	        // B-1 §10.1 ③: never START a settlement that could run out of gas half-way. Reverting here
   440	        // rolls back the user's execution (EntryPoint v0.7 innerHandleOp), so nothing is kept unpaid.
   441	        // GOV-5: the bound is the VALIDATION-time snapshot (trailing word 12), read before
   442	        // decoding and ONLY for a 384-byte context; the admitted limit satisfied MIN_v >= SETTLE_v +
   443	        // 20k, so a parameter change executed mid-bundle cannot move it. Any other length (a 5.5.0
   444	        // context: 352 B) has no snapshot and keeps the 5.5.0 bound.
   445	        uint256 snap;
   446	        if (context.length == CTX_LEN) {
   447	            assembly ("memory-safe") { snap := calldataload(add(context.offset, 352)) }
   448	        }
   449	        uint256 snapSettle = uint32(snap >> 32);
   450	        if (gasleft() < (snapSettle == 0 ? LEGACY_SETTLE_GAS_BOUND : snapSettle)) revert PostOpGasTooLow();
   451	
   452	        OpCtx memory c = abi.decode(context, (OpCtx));
   453	
   454	        // V3.6: rate-limit timestamp ALWAYS (griefing defence), even if the op reverted.
   455	        if (operators[c.operator].minTxInterval > 0) {
   456	            userOpState[c.operator][c.user].lastTimestamp = uint48(block.timestamp);
   457	        }
   458	
   459	        // P1-17 idempotency guard: set before all accounting.
   460	        if (_settledDebtOps[c.opHash]) return;
   461	        _settledDebtOps[c.opHash] = true;
   462	        operators[c.operator].totalTxSponsored++;
   463	
   464	        // R10-M3: conservative charge in wei, priced at the VALIDATION-time snapshot.
   465	        // snapshot: C_POSTOP + C_WRAP of the validation; 5.5.0 context: the 5.5.0 formula itself
   466	        // (postOpGasLimit + LEGACY_C_WRAP), i.e. exactly what that op was admitted and quoted under.
   467	        uint256 bufGas =
   468	            snap == 0 ? uint256(c.postOpGas) + LEGACY_C_WRAP_GAS : uint256(uint32(snap >> 96)) + uint32(snap >> 64);
   469	        uint256 bufWei = (bufGas + Math.ceilDiv((uint256(c.callGas) + c.postOpGas) * 10, 100)) * actualUserOpFeePerGas;
   470	        uint256 aGas = Math.mulDiv(
   471	            (actualGasCost + bufWei) * uint256(c.price),
   472	            1e18,
   473	            (10 ** uint256(c.decimals)) * c.aPriceUSD,
   474	            Math.Rounding.Ceil
   475	        );
   476	        // Fee: the validation-time fee when the context carries one; otherwise (352 B, or 384 B
   477	        // emitted before the fee snapshot) the live fee, which is what that emitter charged.
   478	        uint256 feeSnap = snap >> FEE_SNAP_SHIFT;
   479	        uint256 feeBps = feeSnap == 0 ? protocolFeeBPS : feeSnap - 1;
   480	        uint256 charge = Math.mulDiv(aGas, BPS_DENOMINATOR + feeBps, BPS_DENOMINATOR, Math.Rounding.Ceil);
   481	        if (charge > c.a0) charge = c.a0;
   482	
   483	        // B-1 §10.1 ①: NO try/catch. A failed settlement reverts postOp → EntryPoint rolls back
   484	        // the user's execution; the escrow/reservation is then released after the transaction.
   485	        if (c.mode == MODE_BALANCE) {
   486	            IxPNTsTokenV2(c.token).settleLocked(c.user, c.opHash, charge);
   487	        } else {
   488	            IxPNTsTokenV2(c.token).settleCredit(c.user, c.opHash, charge);
   489	        }
   490	
   491	        // R10-M1b: in-flight a0 → revenue c, refund (a0 − c) to the operator. No shared-pool clamp.
   492	        _clearInflight(c.opHash);
   493	        _setInflightLive(c.opHash, false);
   494	        operators[c.operator].aPNTsBalance += uint128(c.a0 - charge);
   495	        protocolRevenue += charge;
   496	
   497	        emit ISuperPaymaster.TransactionSponsored(c.operator, c.user, aGas, charge);
   498	    }
   499	
   500	    /// @notice R10-M1b: after the original transaction, restore an operator's in-flight a0 whose
   501	    ///         postOp never completed (a postOp revert also rolled back the user's execution).
   502	    ///         Permissionless and idempotent. The EntryPoint ETH for that op stays spent (I10).
   503	    ///         GOV-2: works while sponsorship is paused.
   504	    function releaseStaleSponsorship(bytes32 opHash) external {
   505	        _releaseStaleSponsorship(opHash);
   506	    }
   507	
   508	    function inflightOf(bytes32 opHash) external view returns (address operator, uint256 a0) {
   509	        Inflight memory f = _inflight[opHash];
   510	        return (f.operator, f.a0);
   511	    }
   512	
   513	    function _extractOperator(PackedUserOperation calldata userOp) internal pure returns (address) {
   514	        // paymasterAndData: [paymaster(20)] [gasLimits(32)] [operator(20)] ...
   515	        if (userOp.paymasterAndData.length < 72) return address(0);
   516	        return address(bytes20(userOp.paymasterAndData[PAYMASTER_DATA_OFFSET:PAYMASTER_DATA_OFFSET + 20]));
   517	    }

   520	    // F1: Agent Sponsorship Policy (read inside validation)
   521	    // ====================================

   523	    /// @notice V5.3: Dual-channel eligibility — SBT holder OR registered ERC-8004 agent
   524	    function isEligibleForSponsorship(address user) public view returns (bool) {
   525	        return sbtHolders[user] || isRegisteredAgent(user);
   526	    }

   528	    /// @notice Check if an address is a registered ERC-8004 agent
   529	    /// @dev Called inside validatePaymasterUserOp only when an identity registry is configured.
   530	    ///      Governance MUST opcode- and storage-verify that exact implementation for ERC-7562
   531	    ///      before configuration; this caller cannot prove that its view is environment-opcode-free
   532	    ///      or reads only sender-associated storage. try/catch handles reverts, not rule violations.
   533	    function isRegisteredAgent(address account) public view returns (bool) {
   534	        address reg = agentIdentityRegistry;
   535	        if (reg == address(0)) return false;
   536	        try IAgentIdentityRegistry(reg).isRegisteredAgent(account) returns (bool registered) {
   537	            return registered;
   538	        } catch {
   539	            return false;
   540	        }
   541	    }
